instructions: Cut the ends off the lemon and squeeze them into a small bowl. That should be about 1 tbsp of juice. Slice the rest of the lemon into thin rounds and pick out any seeds. Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.
Lay one chicken breast flat and hold your hand on top. Slice it in half through the side so you have two thin cutlets. Do the same with the other 3 breasts.
Put the cutlets between two sheets of parchment or plastic wrap. Pound them with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until they're about 1/4 inch thick.
In one shallow dish, stir together 1/2 cup of the flour, 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Beat the eggs in a second shallow dish.
Coat a cutlet in the flour and shake off the extra. Dip it in the egg and let the extra drip off. Set it on a plate and do the rest the same way.

Heat the oil in a 12 inch skillet over medium-high for about 2 minutes, until it shimmers. Add 4 cutlets and don't crowd them. Cook for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden, then flip and cook the other side for 3 minutes. Transfer them to a paper towel lined plate and cook the rest.
You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest cutlet. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest one. It's done when there's no pink left.
Pour off most of the oil and wipe out any burnt bits, leaving a thin film in the pan. Lay the lemon slices in the pan over medium-high heat and cook for 30 seconds on each side.
Add the butter. When it melts, sprinkle in the remaining 1 tbsp flour and whisk for 30 seconds.
Pour in the wine, the broth, the 1 tbsp lemon juice and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Scrape up the browned bits and simmer for 2 minutes, until it's slightly thickened.
Return the cutlets to the pan and spoon the sauce over them. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're hot through.
Take the pan off the heat and scatter the parsley over the top. Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve right away with the lemon slices and the pan sauce spooned over the chicken.
method_notes: Jo Cooks (the lead) and Well Plated both flour the cutlets first, then dip them in egg, fry them in batches for about 3 minutes a side, and build the sauce in the same pan from wine, broth and lemon. Jo Cooks seasons the flour, adds a spoonful of flour to the butter to thicken the sauce, and lets the cutlets simmer in it briefly; Well Plated skips the thickener and finishes the sauce with butter and parsley instead. Spend With Pennies adds Parmesan to the egg, which I left out. The lead's measures are kept.
